messages:
devin: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak, we see a small but reproducible regression for long context (>8k) runs when using the ALiBi vectorized kernel on bf16. Loss stays fine on fp32 paths but tokens near the end show NaNs occasionally.

maria: Repro steps? I can try locally.

devin: Minimal repro attached below — runs in our runtime with the vectorized alibi path enabled: 

```py
# repro.py
import torch
from runtime.posenc import apply_alibi  # pseudo import for clarity

x = torch.randn(1, 1, 4096, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
mask = torch.ones(1, 1, 4096, dtype=torch.bool, device='cuda')
# force vectorized kernel selector
torch.set_default_dtype(torch.bfloat16)
out = apply_alibi(x, mask, scale=1.0)
print(out[0,0,-1].sum())
```

It triggers after a few steps in the serving loop — looks like saturating accumulators in the kernel when sequence*heads gets large.

samir: I ran the repro on an A100 with bf16 and got a spike to infs in the attention scores at seq=4096. Switching accumulation to float32 fixes it.

alice: Did we change any scaling constants recently? There was that change to remove a conservative clamp.

devin: Yes — the selector removed the per-head clamp in the optimized path because it added ~0.6% p99 latency in microbenchmarks. That exposed a numerical corner on long tails.

maria: Guessing two viable fixes: 1) do accumulation in fp32 even if inputs are bf16/bf32 (costs some flops/mem), 2) reintroduce a cheap clamp or saturation threshold in the kernel (cheap but heuristic).

samir: Another option: keep bf16 accumulation but add a small pre-scale to keys/queries to keep dot-products in safe range. Like multiply with min(1, scale_threshold/estimated_norm). That's a bit more logic in the kernel selector.

alice: We should also think about testing: add long-seq randomized fuzz tests to catch this earlier. Right now CI uses <=2k sequences.

infra-bot: Perf test queue updated: posenc-longseq-8k enqueued.

devin: Proposed short term plan: re-enable fp32 accumulation for the vectorized alibi kernel under a runtime flag, add a lightweight per-head clamp as guard, and bake a long-seq unit test. Longer-term: add an automatic norm estimator at compile/selection time so kernels pick safe accum mode.

maria: I prototyped the fp32-accum patch — p99 regressed ~2% but no NaNs. I can open a small PR with a runtime flag: `posenc.accum_mode=auto|fp32|bf16` and default to auto.

samir: Can you also measure token throughput with the clamp+bf16-accum combo? If clamp cost is <0.5% maybe that's preferable.

alice: Also add a tiny change to evals: detect upward drift in perplexity or sudden variance spikes for long contexts. That would have caught yesterday's regression earlier.

devin: Good call. For rollout: we'll canary the fp32-accum flag in dedicated pools in eu-west first, run overnight synthetic traffic (8k seq) then extend. Deploy steps in the PR description.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: eng-runtime/canary/posenc-fix -> eu-west-1 at 03:00 UTC.

maria: I will open the PR and include the repro in tests + a small microbenchmark comparing three modes: bf16-accum w/ clamp, bf16-accum no-clamp, fp32-accum.

samir: For the kernel-level clamp, please make it deterministic and explain the constant choice in comments. Something like: `clamp_val = 1e3` is arbitrary; better to base on head_dim and typical init scaling.

devin: Agree — add a function comment: "clamp threshold = k * sqrt(head_dim)" where k chosen from microbench regressions.

alice: Who wants to own the follow-up RFC for a longer-term strategy (accum selection policy + safety tests + selector knobs)? We should capture interface boundaries so product code can request different guarantees (latency vs numerical safety).

maria: I can draft the RFC this week and include compatibility matrix for hosted/dedicated/private (some private installs prefer minimal fp32 use).

devin: Thanks — summary action items: (1) maria PR with fp32-accum flag + tests, (2) microbench of clamp vs fp32 (samir/maria), (3) canary deploy (infra/deploy-bot scheduled), (4) RFC draft (alice/maria) documenting selector policy and knob visibility.

infra-bot: posenc-longseq-8k finished: no regressions on current main in eu-west test cluster (before patch).

samir: Noted — that matches local results. We'll still run canary after PR.

devin: If we get sign-offs fast we can revert the selector change that removed the clamp or flip the default to safe mode. I don't want customer-facing failures.

alice: +1. Keep me posted on the RFC draft and I'll schedule a 30m sync if needed.

maria: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 (WIP) — includes repro, tests, and the runtime flag.

devin: Thanks all. Follow-ups in the PR thread.
